title: Simulation of an oracle query
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean oracle Turing machine and $C$ a Boolean multitape Turing machine with $c>0$ work tapes, and choose states $en,ex$ of $C$ and an oracle language $O$. Let $c_0$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$ whose state is the query state. Choose a side tag $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ such that the query-tape head position $p$ satisfies $p\ge 0$ when $b=\mathrm{true}$ and $p\le 0$ when $b=\mathrm{false}$, and suppose the query tape is blank at some cell $r\ge0$. Write $z$ for the query string on that tape. Suppose that from the standard configuration of $C$ in state $en$ with $z$ on its first work tape and all other tapes blank, the machine reaches the standard configuration in state $ex$ with the one-symbol word recording whether $z\in O$ after $t$ steps, and does not visit state $ex$ earlier. Then the host machine built from $M$ and $C$, started in the stable encoding of $c_0$ with tag $b$, reaches after some $u\le 2|p|+2|z|+t+13$ steps the stable encoding of the oracle-step successor of $c_0$ for some tag $b'$; the successor query-tape head position satisfies the corresponding side condition for $b'$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean oracle machine M and Boolean multitape machine C
chosen entry and exit states en, ex
c₀ is in the query state
side tag and orientation condition on query-tape head position
query tape is blank at a nonnegative cell r
C's computation on the query string reaches the specified one-symbol answer configuration after t steps
C avoids the exit state at every earlier step
natural-number bound on host simulation time u
